lady to her patient at l. 42, where Jane is also named in the MS). At some point Jane’s
MS was acquired by Trelawny, who showed it to Rossetti as the basis for his emended text
in Rossetti 1870, which for the first time gave the correct title, and restored ‘Jane’ in the last
line (for the Athenaeum’s ‘friend’: Rossetti 1870 ii 286–288, 576–577). On Trelawny’s death
the MS passed to his daughter Mrs Laetitia Call, who in turn presented it to the Bodleian
Library in 1907 (MS Shelley adds. e. 3, ff. 1–3r).
 With a guitar. To Jane is amongst the most subtle and sophisticated of S’s late lyrics,
suggesting, as do the Jane poems as a group, an influence from English Renaissance poetry.
